title: Enhancing graduate students’ evaluative skills through AI-supported collaborative marking
extended_summary:
This paper investigates how AI-supported collaborative marking can improve graduate students’ evaluative judgment when assessing research papers. The authors argue that prior AI-assisted assessment research has focused too heavily on score accuracy and agreement with human raters, while paying less attention to how interaction with AI may shape students’ reasoning, monitoring, and reflection during evaluation.

The study tests a collaborative marking framework in which students evaluate their own research papers with support from an AI agent grounded in an expert-informed knowledge base and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). The AI system provides rubric-based feedback on four dimensions: rigor, originality, significance, and conventions. The population consisted of 121 first-year master’s students at Hubei University in China, who produced and self-evaluated approximately 8,000-word research papers as part of an AI in Education course. The study compared four conditions: student-only marking, AI-only marking, AI with RAG, and AI-supported collaborative marking. A smaller subset of students was also used for behavioral coding and lag sequential analysis of interaction logs.

Findings showed that AI-supported collaborative marking reduced deviations from expert ratings and improved consistency relative to student-only and AI-only conditions. The authors also found that students’ interaction patterns reflected differences in metacognitive monitoring and reflective reasoning, with senior students showing more structured and self-regulated evaluative behavior than junior students. Overall, the paper concludes that AI-supported collaborative marking can improve assessment accuracy while also supporting the development of academic assessment literacy and evaluative judgment in graduate education.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a mixed-method, single-study comparison with within-subject and benchmark comparisons, not an RCT or meta-analysis. It provides empirical evidence with reasonable structure and reliability reporting, but the design has important limitations for causal inference and general K-12 relevance.
impact_tier_rationale: The observed improvement in marking accuracy is meaningful for the studied graduate population, but the context is higher education rather than K-12 and the evidence is specific to writing evaluation. The main effect reported is moderate in practical terms, but generalizable impact for the requested K-12 science-focused evidence base is unclear.

interventions.use_case: AI-supported collaborative marking of graduate research papers using rubric-based scoring and feedback, including expert-knowledge retrieval augmentation and discrepancy checking against expert benchmarks
A conversational AI agent (DeepSeek-V3.1-Terminus) that interacts with students during marking, prompts justification and reflection, and supports iterative calibration of scores

finding.finding_summary: AI-supported collaborative marking improved evaluative judgment and metacognitive regulation compared with student-only and AI-only conditions. The paper reports a reduction in mean absolute error from 3.260 to 1.221 versus expert ratings in the collaborative condition, alongside improved inter-rater consistency and more structured planning-monitoring-reflection cycles.
finding.measure: Deviation from expert ratings on rubric-based paper evaluation; inter-rater consistency; behavioral interaction patterns
finding.study_size: n=121 papers; n=121 student evaluators; interaction subset n=12 students / 269 coded events

finding.finding_summary: The intervention targeted assessment of academic writing quality across rigor, originality, significance, and conventions, and collaborative marking produced scores closer to expert benchmarks. Student ratings were especially improved relative to expert judgments on paper conventions and overall scoring accuracy, with MAE decreasing from 3.260 to 1.221 in the collaborative condition.
finding.measure: Rubric-based scores for research paper quality (rigor, originality, significance, conventions) and overall mark

finding.finding_summary: The AI-supported condition was associated with increased reflective engagement and self-regulated evaluation rather than mere score generation. Behavioral coding showed senior students more often engaged in metacognitive monitoring, reflective reasoning, and structured regulation, indicating that the collaborative process supported more adaptive engagement with the task.
finding.measure: Behavioral coding of interaction logs; qualitative/lag sequential analysis of AI-supported marking dialogue
